summary: This bill amends the Social Security Act to bar states from providing Medicaid coverage starting in 2026 to able-bodied adults who fail to work or volunteer at least 20 hours per week on average, while exempting those under 18 or over 65, pregnant individuals, primary caretakers of young or disabled children, and certain others.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes work requirements on able-bodied adults in Medicaid, which would reduce program enrollment and expenditures by limiting eligibility for non-compliant individuals. This directly aims to curb government spending on the Medicaid program.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.

The bill modifies Medicaid eligibility by adding work requirements, thereby restricting access to this public coverage program. This moves the system slightly toward limiting public benefits in favor of encouraging private employment or self-sufficiency.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, border policy, or pathways for non-citizens.
No provisions address reproductive health services, abortion access, or related funding restrictions.
No provisions involve military, defense, or national security spending.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy production.

The bill directly restricts Medicaid eligibility for able-bodied adults via work requirements, scaling back access to this major safety-net program (with specified exemptions). This aligns with efforts to reduce welfare program participation.
No provisions address schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
The bill includes an exemption for individuals in drug addiction or alcoholic treatment programs but does not otherwise alter drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reforms.
No provisions relate to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
By reducing Medicaid expenditures through eligibility restrictions, the bill would modestly contribute to lower deficit spending, aligning with debt-reduction priorities.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions involve foreign aid, international assistance, or related funding.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or voter ID requirements.
No provisions relate to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address union rights, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights protections, or anti-discrimination rules.
